thread.title: Tech Today: Trade Desk Soars, Nvidia's Crypto Thing, Symantec Crumbles

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Trade Desk Soars, Nvidia's Crypto Thing, Symantec Crumbles
text:
Here are some things going on today in ;the world of tech :
Shares of security technology giant Symantec ( SYMC ) are down $9.98, or 34%, at $19.20, after it said yesterday afternoon that its board has opened an investigation into its accounting "in connection with concerns raised by a former employee." The investigation could lead to a revision of the company's financial reports from the past.
The announcement came in conjunction with fiscal Q4 results that beat expectations, but a forecast for this quarter, and the year, that was below consensus.
The stock this morning has gotten at least eight downgrades .
Andrew Nowinski ;of Piper Jaffray , cutting his rating to Neutral from Overweight, and slashing his target to $24 from $32, writes that "this investigation creates too much uncertainty to have confidence in management's FY19 guidance, as this could affect historical results and future demand trends."
Bears are not inclined to pile in amidst the stock implosion. Anne Meisner of Susquehanna ;writes that the "long overdue estimate reset combined with last night's aftermarket levels of around $23 would presumably provide for a better setup for SYMC."
"However, the risk of a negative outcome of the investigation keeps us on the sidelines."
The ;'Crypto Thing' ;C ontinues to Hurt Nvidia
Chip giant Nvidia ;( NVDA ) shares are down $4.90, or 1.9%, at $255.28, despite the company yesterday reporting fiscal Q1 ;revenue and profit that crushed expectations, and an outlook for this quarter similarly bright.
Price targets are rising at several shops, but the blemish, to some, is that crypto currency ;again showed up as a driver of the quarter-something that worries some analysts because of its volatility.
The company actually disclosed the amount of crypto, which it hasn't always done, noting it added up to $289 million ;in the quarter.
Deutsche Bank 's Ross Seymore keeps his Hold rating on the stock, while raising his price target to $260 from $240, writing that the quality of the beat was less than in some other quarters because crypto contributed to some of the beat, and because there was " channel fill " of videogaming GPUs.
But Hans Mosesmann ;with Rosenblatt , reiterating his Buy rating, and raising his price target to $315 from $300, writes that "the crypto thing is no longer a relevant bear theme in our opinion. Get over it."
Rather, "Nvidia continues to execute flawlessly in its target markets and we are in the early days of the Volta GPU disruption in the data- center."
Trade Desk Soars
Shares of advertising software maker ;Trade Desk ;( TTD ) are up $19.11, or over 36%, at $71.85, after it beat expectations comfortably , and beat with this quarter's, and the full year's, outlook.
As Chief Executive Jeff ;Green ;predicted in my chat with him last night, this morning's looking "pretty good" for the stock.
Here, too, price targets are going sharply higher. Mark Mahaney ;of RBC Capital , reiterating an Outperform rating, raises his target to $80 from $67, writing that "this was an inflection point quarter for TTD, with revenue growth accelerating 19pts to 60%+ and Ebitda margin expanding 10-pts Y/Y.
"It's clear to us that Digital/Programmatic advertising adoption is accelerating, and TTD is an industry leader."
Defending Talend
Cloud-software maker Talend ;( TLND ) is down $4.27, or 7%, at $55.30, after it slightly beat revenue expectations but missed by a penny on the bottom line because of an accounting change.
Bulls this morning are unfazed by that accounting matter. Needham & Co .'s Jack Andrews , reiterating a Buy rating, raises his price target to $64 from $59. He notes that the company's deferred revenue was also held back by the accounting issue, declining by $3.6 million. But if one excludes the impact of the rule, " IFRS 15 ," deferred revenue would have been up $2 million, "consistent with prior quarters."
More important to Andrews is that "cloud migrations" for Talend's customers are making a meaningful impact on its revenue mix . "Big data and cloud integration products represented more than 50% of subscription revenue, up from 40% in the previous quarter," he notes."
Tesla Versus the Boneheads
Bulls on Tesla ( TSLA ) are still defending the company after last week's temper tantrum by CEO Elon Musk ;on the conference call with analysts.
Instinet 's Romit Shah , who has a Buy rating on the shares, and a $420 price target, today issues a slide deck titled " don't be a bonehead ," a reference to the insult Musk dished out to analysts on that call.
Shah offers slides ;showing all the relevant data as he sees them - including the potential for Tesla to take 10% of the luxury car market by 2022 . The top three brands in luxury have 20% apiece, which means that there's share "ripe for the picking," in his view.
"Tesla is one of the most shorted stocks in the US stock market; however we believe that over the next 3-6 months the narrative on the company will shift from insolvency risk and cash burn to market opportunity and growth."
Tesla stock today is down $1.19, or 0.4%, at $303.83.
T-Mobile and Sprint
Instinet's Jeffrey Kvaal ;today gives an update on the prospects for T-Mobile US 's (TMUS) proposed merger with Sprint (S), after hosting lunch yesterday with T-Mo investor relations and a group of investors.
"We came away encouraged to hear the Sprint deal is finding receptivity in some DC circles," he writes, "though we believe the odds are long."
Kvaal relates that "initial conversations with lawmakers suggest the deal will get a fair hearing."
"Key milestones include the June 12th date for a ruling in the AT&T case, an S-4 filing in early summer, followed by the official FCC review timeline."
"We expect the FCC process to be more open and transparent than the DoJ process. While 12-18 months out from resolution, we still believe the regulatory hurdle to be high with likelihood of approval well below 50%."
T-Mobile shares today are down 30 cents, or 0.5%, at $56.55.
Apple Keeps Rising
Shares of Apple ;(AAPL), on ;their way to $1 trillion in market capitalization, ;are down from ;their new all-time intraday high yesterday of $190.37, but are up 9 cents today at $189.39.
